tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use when a customer reports a MediaLive problem or when evidence points at the encoding layer...'), focuses on the triggering scenarios/user intent (customer reports, evidence pointing at encoding layer) rather than internal implementation, explicitly lists many trigger contexts (input loss, dropped frames, fill/black frames, active alerts, output errors, pipeline desync, schedule/SCTE-35 anomalies, specific input types), and also explicitly scopes out-of-domain cases to other skills. It is a dense but bounded paragraph appropriate for the complexity of the domain.
tests.evidence: Use when a customer reports a MediaLive problem or when evidence points at the encoding layer: input loss, dropped frames, fill or black frames in output, active alerts, output 4xx/5xx push errors, pipeline desynchronization on STANDARD channels, or schedule and input-switch anomalies, including SCTE-35 schedule actions.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (exact CLI commands, metric dimensions, state interpretation) are prescriptive, while findings compilation and escalation phrasing give flexibility with rationale (e.g., 'Do not declare a definitive root cause; surface evidence and the precise question').
tests.evidence: Structure each finding as Observed (the value plus the API or metric it came from), Expected (the threshold or benchmark plus its source), and Question: why? Do not declare a definitive root cause; surface evidence and the precise question that follows from it.
